objects.description: Opaque version/revision info record returned by gsapi_revision(). Holds product/copyright strings and numeric revision/date identifiers.
Forward declaration for the display device callback structure used by the (deprecated) display device API. Actual fields are defined elsewhere (gdevdisp.h).
Forward declaration for Ghostscript memory manager object. Definition resides elsewhere; used here only as an opaque handle in file-system hook callbacks.
Forward declaration for Ghostscript platform file handle wrapper. Definition is elsewhere (gp.h); used opaquely in file-system hook callbacks.

Callback vtable for plugging a custom filesystem into Ghostscript. Each function returns a gs error code and yields a gp_file* on success. rfname/fname buffers are expected to be up to gp_file_name_sizeof (4096) bytes. The secret pointer is an opaque per-registration cookie. Lifetime is owned by the embedding app; register with gsapi_add_fs() and remove with gsapi_remove_fs().

Function-pointer type for device-specific callouts from Ghostscript to the host. Returns a Ghostscript error code (negative for error, 0/positive for success; return gs_error_unknownerror (-1) to indicate unclaimed). Register/deregister via gsapi_register_callout/gsapi_deregister_callout.

objects.definition:
typedef enum {
    gs_spt_invalid = -1,
    gs_spt_null    = 0,
    gs_spt_bool    = 1,
    gs_spt_int     = 2,
    gs_spt_float   = 3,
    gs_spt_name    = 4,
    gs_spt_string  = 5,
    gs_spt_long    = 6,
    gs_spt_i64     = 7,
    gs_spt_size_t  = 8,
    gs_spt_parsed  = 9,
    gs_spt_more_to_come = 1<<31
} gs_set_param_type;
objects.description: Enumeration describing parameter value types for gsapi_set_param/get_param/enumerate_params. Values identify the pointed-to type; gs_spt_more_to_come is an OR-able flag to defer device reinitialization across batches of sets.
Anonymous enum constants indicating the argument string encoding used with gsapi_set_arg_encoding(). Not a distinct named type; treated as ints.
Anonymous enum constants selecting which permission set to modify for path control APIs (reading, writing, or file control). Not a distinct named type; treated as ints.

functions.name: gsapi_revision
functions.signature: GSDLLEXPORT int GSDLLAPI gsapi_revision(gsapi_revision_t *pr, int len);
functions.description: Returns Ghostscript product/revision information into the supplied gsapi_revision_t. Safe to call at any time, and recommended to call first to verify the linked GS version. If len is too small for the current structure, the function returns the required size instead of 0.
requirements: pr must be a valid, writable pointer to a gsapi_revision_t (or a compatible larger struct).
len should be the size in bytes of the structure pointed to by pr.
On success, returns 0; if len is too small, returns the required size in bytes.
May be called before creating any Ghostscript instance.

functions.name: gsapi_new_instance
functions.signature: GSDLLEXPORT int GSDLLAPI gsapi_new_instance(void **pinstance, void *caller_handle);
functions.description: Creates a new Ghostscript interpreter instance for subsequent API calls. The caller_handle is stored and provided back to callbacks (stdio, poll, callouts, etc.). On some platforms only one instance is supported; a second attempt will fail with <0 and set *pinstance to NULL.
requirements: pinstance must be non-NULL and point to a void* location to receive the instance handle.
On non-threading-capable platforms only a single instance is allowed; a second creation attempt returns < 0 and sets *pinstance to NULL.
Call this before any other gsapi_… function that requires an instance.
Store the returned instance pointer for all further calls and for deletion.

functions.name: gsapi_delete_instance
functions.signature: GSDLLEXPORT void GSDLLAPI gsapi_delete_instance(void *instance);
functions.description: Destroys a Ghostscript interpreter instance and releases associated resources. Must be the final call for an instance.
requirements: instance must be a valid instance previously returned by gsapi_new_instance.
If the instance was initialised via gsapi_init_with_args, you must call gsapi_exit(instance) before gsapi_delete_instance.
Only call after Ghostscript has finished processing (no further run calls).
Do not use the instance after deletion.

functions.name: gsapi_set_stdio
functions.signature: GSDLLEXPORT int GSDLLAPI gsapi_set_stdio(void *instance, int (GSDLLCALLPTR stdin_fn)(void *caller_handle, char *buf, int len), int (GSDLLCALLPTR stdout_fn)(void *caller_handle, const char *str, int len), int (GSDLLCALLPTR stderr_fn)(void *caller_handle, const char *str, int len));
functions.description: Registers callback functions to handle stdin, stdout, and stderr for the interpreter. If any callback is NULL, real stdio is used for that stream. Return values from callbacks are used directly by Ghostscript.
requirements: instance must be a valid instance created by gsapi_new_instance.
stdin_fn, if provided, must return: number of bytes read on success, 0 on EOF, or -1 on error; it will be passed a writable buffer of length len.
stdout_fn and stderr_fn, if provided, must return the number of characters written.
Callbacks receive the caller_handle given at gsapi_new_instance.
Set callbacks before initialising the interpreter for consistent behavior.

functions.name: gsapi_set_stdio_with_handle
functions.signature: GSDLLEXPORT int GSDLLAPI gsapi_set_stdio_with_handle(void *instance, int (GSDLLCALLPTR stdin_fn)(void *caller_handle, char *buf, int len), int (GSDLLCALLPTR stdout_fn)(void *caller_handle, const char *str, int len), int (GSDLLCALLPTR stderr_fn)(void *caller_handle, const char *str, int len), void *caller_handle);
functions.description: Like gsapi_set_stdio, but associates a specific caller_handle for these callbacks instead of the default handle supplied at instance creation.
requirements: instance must be a valid instance.
Callback contracts are identical to gsapi_set_stdio regarding return values and buffer handling.
caller_handle will be supplied to the callbacks registered by this call.
Set before interpreter initialisation for consistent behavior.

functions.name: gsapi_set_poll
functions.signature: GSDLLEXPORT int GSDLLAPI gsapi_set_poll(void *instance, int (GSDLLCALLPTR poll_fn)(void *caller_handle));
functions.description: Registers a polling callback used for window event handling or cooperative multitasking. Only called if Ghostscript was compiled with CHECK_INTERRUPTS. The function must be fast; returning a negative value requests Ghostscript to abort.
requirements: instance must be a valid instance.
poll_fn must be fast and re-entrant enough for frequent polling.
poll_fn must return 0 to continue; a negative value requests Ghostscript to abort.
Callback receives the caller_handle set at instance creation.
Effective only if Ghostscript is built with CHECK_INTERRUPTS (as per gpcheck.h).

functions.name: gsapi_set_poll_with_handle
functions.signature: GSDLLEXPORT int GSDLLEXPORT gsapi_set_poll_with_handle(void *instance, int (GSDLLCALLPTR poll_fn)(void *caller_handle), void *caller_handle);
functions.description: Registers a polling callback like gsapi_set_poll, but uses the specified caller_handle for this registration.
requirements: instance must be valid.
poll_fn must be fast; return 0 to continue, negative to request abort.
caller_handle will be passed to poll_fn.
Only effective if Ghostscript was compiled with CHECK_INTERRUPTS.

functions.name: gsapi_set_display_callback
functions.signature: GSDLLEXPORT int GSDLLAPI gsapi_set_display_callback(void *instance, display_callback *callback);
functions.description: Sets the display device callback structure for use with the display device. Must be called after creating the instance and before initialising with arguments. Deprecated in favor of gsapi_register_callout.
requirements: instance must be valid.
callback must point to a properly populated display_callback structure (see gdevdisp.h for details).
Call after gsapi_new_instance() and before gsapi_init_with_args().
Deprecated: prefer gsapi_register_callout for new code.

functions.name: gsapi_register_callout
functions.signature: GSDLLEXPORT int GSDLLAPI gsapi_register_callout(void *instance, gs_callout callout, void *callout_handle);
functions.description: Registers a device callout handler to allow devices to query the caller in device-specific ways. The handler is called with device name, id, size, and data and should return standard Ghostscript error codes (non-negative on success; gs_error_unknownerror (-1) if unclaimed).
requirements: instance must be valid.
callout must be a valid function pointer of type gs_callout.
Should be called after gsapi_new_instance() and typically before gsapi_init_with_args().
callout will be passed the provided callout_handle on invocation.

functions.name: gsapi_deregister_callout
functions.signature: GSDLLEXPORT void GSDLLAPI gsapi_deregister_callout(void *instance, gs_callout callout, void *callout_handle);
functions.description: Unregisters a previously registered callout handler for the specified instance and handle.
requirements: instance must be valid.
callout and callout_handle must match a prior registration to ensure deregistration of the intended handler.

functions.name: gsapi_set_default_device_list
functions.signature: GSDLLEXPORT int GSDLLAPI gsapi_set_default_device_list(void *instance, const char *list, int listlen);
functions.description: Sets the string containing a space-separated list of default device names (e.g., "display x11alpha x11 bbox"). Influences which device(s) Ghostscript will try to select the default device. Must be set before interpreter initialisation.
requirements: instance must be valid.
list must point to a buffer containing the device list; listlen is the length of the list in bytes.
Must be called after gsapi_new_instance() and before gsapi_init_with_args().

functions.name: gsapi_get_default_device_list
functions.signature: GSDLLEXPORT int GSDLLAPI gsapi_get_default_device_list(void *instance, char **list, int *listlen);
functions.description: Retrieves a pointer to the current default device list string and its length.
requirements: instance must be valid.
list must be a valid pointer to receive a char*; listlen must be a valid pointer to receive the length in bytes.
Must be called after gsapi_new_instance().
The lifetime/ownership of the returned string is managed by Ghostscript; do not free it (implicit from typical API pattern; no alternative stated).

functions.name: gsapi_set_arg_encoding
functions.signature: GSDLLEXPORT int GSDLLAPI gsapi_set_arg_encoding(void *instance, int encoding);
functions.description: Sets the character encoding used for API argument strings (argv, parameters, etc.). Defaults to a platform 'local' encoding (Windows codepage, Linux UTF-8). Use of 'local' encoding with this API is now deprecated.
requirements: instance must be valid.
encoding must be one of: GS_ARG_ENCODING_LOCAL (0), GS_ARG_ENCODING_UTF8 (1), GS_ARG_ENCODING_UTF16LE (2).
Call before passing strings in the selected encoding to other functions.

functions.name: gsapi_init_with_args
functions.signature: GSDLLEXPORT int GSDLLAPI gsapi_init_with_args(void *instance, int argc, char **argv);
functions.description: Initialises the interpreter with the given command-line-like arguments. Typical flow: call this once, then run one or more gsapi_run_* functions, then call gsapi_exit. Special return values indicate Quit or Info conditions rather than errors.
requirements: instance must be valid.
argc and argv must describe a valid argument vector (argv may be modified/consumed by Ghostscript depending on build).
If this returns gs_error_Quit, you must call gsapi_exit() and must not call other gsapi_* functions first.
If this returns gs_error_Info, usage info should be displayed; do not call gsapi_exit().
On normal success returns 0; proceed to gsapi_run_* calls, then finish with gsapi_exit().
Call only once per instance (implied by typical interpreter lifecycle).

functions.name: gsapi_run_string_begin
functions.signature: GSDLLEXPORT int GSDLLAPI gsapi_run_string_begin(void *instance, int user_errors, int *pexit_code);
functions.description: Begins a string-based run session, preparing to feed PostScript/PDF code via subsequent gsapi_run_string_continue calls, finalized by gsapi_run_string_end.
requirements: instance must be initialised via gsapi_init_with_args before running.
pexit_code must be a valid pointer to receive interpreter exit status.
user_errors determines whether errors are returned to the caller or handled internally (semantics follow Ghostscript conventions).
If this or subsequent run calls return <= -100, treat as quit/fatal and call gsapi_exit() next.

functions.name: gsapi_run_string_continue
functions.signature: GSDLLEXPORT int GSDLLAPI gsapi_run_string_continue(void *instance, const char *str, unsigned int length, int user_errors, int *pexit_code);
functions.description: Continues feeding a chunk of code to an ongoing string run begun with gsapi_run_string_begin. Returns gs_error_NeedInput to indicate more input is required when all is well.
requirements: instance must be in a begun run (after gsapi_run_string_begin).
str must point to the next data chunk; length is the number of bytes to process.
pexit_code must be a valid pointer to receive status.
If return value <= -100, quit/fatal occurred; call gsapi_exit() next.
Expect gs_error_NeedInput on normal continuation when more input is desired.

functions.name: gsapi_run_string_end
functions.signature: GSDLLEXPORT int GSDLLAPI gsapi_run_string_end(void *instance, int user_errors, int *pexit_code);
functions.description: Ends a string-based run session started with gsapi_run_string_begin, finalising interpretation of accumulated input.
requirements: instance must have a matching gsapi_run_string_begin sequence in progress.
pexit_code must be valid to receive status.
If return value <= -100, quit/fatal occurred; call gsapi_exit() next.

functions.name: gsapi_run_string_with_length
functions.signature: GSDLLEXPORT int GSDLLAPI gsapi_run_string_with_length(void *instance, const char *str, unsigned int length, int user_errors, int *pexit_code);
functions.description: Runs a single string buffer of the specified length through the interpreter in one call.
requirements: instance must be initialised via gsapi_init_with_args.
str must not be NULL; length is the number of bytes to execute.
pexit_code must be valid.
If return value <= -100, quit/fatal occurred; call gsapi_exit() next.

functions.name: gsapi_run_string
functions.signature: GSDLLEXPORT int GSDLLAPI gsapi_run_string(void *instance, const char *str, int user_errors, int *pexit_code);
functions.description: Runs a NUL-terminated string through the interpreter in one call.
requirements: instance must be initialised via gsapi_init_with_args.
str must be a valid NUL-terminated string.
pexit_code must be valid.
If return value <= -100, quit/fatal occurred; call gsapi_exit() next.

functions.name: gsapi_run_file
functions.signature: GSDLLEXPORT int GSDLLAPI gsapi_run_file(void *instance, const char *file_name, int user_errors, int *pexit_code);
functions.description: Loads and runs the specified file via the interpreter. Processes PostScript/PDF or other supported content.
requirements: instance must be initialised via gsapi_init_with_args.
file_name must be a pointer to a valid NUL-terminated path string.
pexit_code must be valid.
If return value <= -100, quit/fatal occurred; call gsapi_exit() next.

functions.name: gsapi_exit
functions.signature: GSDLLEXPORT int GSDLLAPI gsapi_exit(void *instance);
functions.description: Shuts down the interpreter for the given instance. Must be called if gsapi_init_with_args() succeeded and just before deleting the instance.
requirements: instance must be valid.
Must be called once after a successful gsapi_init_with_args() and before gsapi_delete_instance().
Do not make further gsapi_run_* calls after exit; the interpreter is no longer active.

functions.name: gsapi_set_param
functions.signature: GSDLLEXPORT int GSDLLAPI gsapi_set_param(void *instance, const char *param, const void *value, gs_set_param_type type);
functions.description: Sets a device or interpreter parameter by name with a typed value. Typed params are typically sent immediately to the device (which may cause reinitialisation). If type is ORed with gs_spt_more_to_come, the update is deferred until a subsequent non-more_to_come set or device init. Allows complex values via gs_spt_parsed.
requirements: instance must be valid.
param must be a valid NUL-terminated key name.

value must point to storage matching the specified type: for gs_spt_bool/int/long/i64/size_t value points to the corresponding integer type; for gs_spt_float a float*; for gs_spt_name/string a char* (NUL-terminated); for gs_spt_parsed a pointer to a char* to be parsed.
When using gs_spt_more_to_come, only valid for set_param (not for get).
Caller should be aware that setting typed params can trigger device reinitialisation immediately unless gs_spt_more_to_come is used.
Return value is a Ghostscript error code; 0 on success, negative on error.

functions.name: gsapi_get_param
functions.signature: GSDLLEXPORT int GSDLLAPI gsapi_get_param(void *instance, const char *param, void *value, gs_set_param_type type);
functions.description: Retrieves a parameter value by name into caller-provided storage. If value is NULL on entry, returns the byte size required for the storage of the given type. For name/string/parsed types, the returned string is NUL-terminated and the size includes the terminator. Returns gs_error_undefined (-21) if not found.
requirements: instance must be valid.
param must be a valid key name.
type must specify the expected storage type; value must point to appropriately sized writable storage for that type, or be NULL to query the required size.
For name/string/parsed, call first with value=NULL to obtain size, then allocate storage and call again to retrieve the NUL-terminated string.
Interpret return value: negative on error; -21 specifically indicates not found; non-negative indicates success or size requirement.

functions.name: gsapi_enumerate_params
functions.signature: GSDLLEXPORT int GSDLLAPI gsapi_enumerate_params(void *instance, void **iterator, const char **key, gs_set_param_type *type);
functions.description: Enumerates all available parameters. The caller maintains an iterator (void*) initially NULL; each call updates it and returns the next key and type. Returns 0 on success, 1 when no more keys, negative on error.
requirements: instance must be valid.
*iterator must be initialised to NULL before the first call, and the same pointer passed back on subsequent calls; the function updates it in place.
key must be a valid pointer to receive a transient const char*; it is valid only until the next call.
type must be a valid pointer to receive the gs_set_param_type for the key.
Only one enumeration may be active at a time; starting a new one invalidates any previous enumeration state.

functions.name: gsapi_add_control_path
functions.signature: GSDLLEXPORT int GSDLLAPI gsapi_add_control_path(void *instance, int type, const char *path);
functions.description: Adds a path to one of the sets of permitted filesystem paths for reading, writing, or file control, according to the type selector.
requirements: instance must be valid.
type must be one of: GS_PERMIT_FILE_READING (0), GS_PERMIT_FILE_WRITING (1), GS_PERMIT_FILE_CONTROL (2).
path must be a valid NUL-terminated path string.

functions.name: gsapi_remove_control_path
functions.signature: GSDLLEXPORT int GSDLLAPI gsapi_remove_control_path(void *instance, int type, const char *path);
functions.description: Removes a path from one of the sets of permitted filesystem paths previously added with gsapi_add_control_path.
requirements: instance must be valid.
type must be one of: GS_PERMIT_FILE_READING (0), GS_PERMIT_FILE_WRITING (1), GS_PERMIT_FILE_CONTROL (2).
path must be a valid NUL-terminated path string corresponding to an existing entry.

functions.name: gsapi_purge_control_paths
functions.signature: GSDLLEXPORT void GSDLLAPI gsapi_purge_control_paths(void *instance, int type);
functions.description: Clears all paths from one of the permitted-path sets designated by type.
requirements: instance must be valid.
type must be one of: GS_PERMIT_FILE_READING (0), GS_PERMIT_FILE_WRITING (1), GS_PERMIT_FILE_CONTROL (2).

functions.name: gsapi_activate_path_control
functions.signature: GSDLLEXPORT void GSDLLAPI gsapi_activate_path_control(void *instance, int enable);
functions.description: Globally enables or disables the path control mechanism that enforces the permitted path sets.
requirements: instance must be valid.
enable should be non-zero to enable path control, zero to disable (integer flag).

functions.name: gsapi_is_path_control_active
functions.signature: GSDLLEXPORT int GSDLLAPI gsapi_is_path_control_active(void *instance);
functions.description: Returns non-zero if path control is currently active for the given instance; zero if inactive.
requirements: instance must be valid.

functions.name: gsapi_add_fs
functions.signature: GSDLLEXPORT int GSDLLAPI gsapi_add_fs(void *instance, gsapi_fs_t *fs, void *secret);
functions.description: Adds a filesystem provider (set of open_* hooks) to Ghostscript. Allows the host to intercept or implement file/pipeline/printer/handle opening operations; the secret pointer is passed back to the hooks.
requirements: instance must be valid.
fs must point to a valid gsapi_fs_t structure whose function pointers adhere to their declared calling conventions and buffer size contracts (e.g., rfname buffers are 4096 bytes).
secret is an opaque pointer passed back to the fs hooks unchanged.

functions.name: gsapi_remove_fs
functions.signature: GSDLLEXPORT void GSDLLAPI gsapi_remove_fs(void *instance, gsapi_fs_t *fs, void *secret);
functions.description: Removes a previously added filesystem provider from Ghostscript.
requirements: instance must be valid.
fs and secret must match a previously added filesystem provider to ensure removal of the intended entry.

unharnessable_functions.name: gsapi_set_display_callback
unharnessable_functions.reason: display_callback structure layout is opaque and not provided here, so a valid, populated callback table cannot be safely constructed for registration.

data_types.description: A single string containing one or more Ghostscript device identifiers separated by spaces (e.g., "display x11alpha bbox"). Tokens are device names recognized by Ghostscript.
Strings intended to emulate argv entries passed to Ghostscript initialisation. Each is an arbitrary argument token, which may include options (e.g., -sDEVICE=pdfwrite), switches, or filenames.
Arbitrary byte sequences intended to be executed by the Ghostscript interpreter as PostScript or PDF content supplied via string-based run APIs.
A filename pointing to a file whose contents are interpreted by Ghostscript as PostScript, PDF, or other supported document formats.
A NUL-terminated string naming a Ghostscript parameter (e.g., "PageSize", "HWResolution"). Used in get/set parameter APIs.
A NUL-terminated string used as a value for string/name/parsed parameter types when setting Ghostscript parameters. Content varies by parameter semantics.
A NUL-terminated path string indicating a directory or file location on the host filesystem, used for path control APIs to permit or remove access.

generators.generator:
import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for: space-separated device names string passed to gsapi_set_default_device_list
# Requirements: Non-empty, space-separated Ghostscript device identifiers. Aim to produce
# a variety of plausible device lists that exercise code paths (single device, multiple,
# repeated tokens, unknown tokens mixed in, case variations, with/without trailing spaces).

KNOWN_DEVICES = [
    # Common display and raster devices
    "display", "x11", "x11alpha", "x11cmyk", "x11rg16x", "bmpmono", "bmpgray",
    "bmp16", "bmp256", "bmp16m", "pngmono", "pnggray", "png16", "png256", "png16m",
    "pngalpha", "jpeg", "jpegcmyk", "jpeggray", "tiffgray", "tiff12nc", "tiff24nc",
    "tiff32nc", "tiffsep", "tiffsep1", "tifflzw", "tiffpack", "tiffcrle",
    # Vector/other
    "pdfwrite", "ps2write", "eps2write", "bbox", "inkcov", "bit", "bitrgb", "bitcmyk",
    # Printers/spool
    "cups", "ijs", "bjc600", "bjc800", "ljet2p", "ljet3", "ljet3d", "ljet4", "deskjet",
]

# Some intentionally odd but syntactically valid tokens to mix in
UNKNOWN_TOKENS = [
    "foo", "bar", "qux", "devX", "x11alpha2", "mydevice", "PDFWRITE", "Display",
]

# Case variants generator
def vary_case(token: str, rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Randomly apply upper/lower/mixed case to explore case handling
    mode = rng.choice(["lower", "upper", "mixed", "as_is"])  # as_is preserves token
    if mode == "lower":
        return token.lower()
    if mode == "upper":
        return token.upper()
    if mode == "mixed":
        return "".join(ch.upper() if rng.random() < 0.5 else ch.lower() for ch in token)
    return token

def build_device_list(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Decide how many tokens
    count_mode = rng.random()
    if count_mode < 0.2:
        n = 1
    elif count_mode < 0.6:
        n = rng.randint(2, 4)
    else:
        n = rng.randint(5, 12)

    tokens: List[str] = []

    # Bias towards known devices but sometimes include unknowns
    for _ in range(n):
        if rng.random() < 0.8:
            tok = rng.choice(KNOWN_DEVICES)
        else:
            tok = rng.choice(UNKNOWN_TOKENS)
        tok = vary_case(tok, rng)
        tokens.append(tok)

    # Occasionally add duplicates to test de-duplication/selection behavior
    if rng.random() < 0.3 and tokens:
        dup = rng.choice(tokens)
        insert_pos = rng.randrange(0, len(tokens) + 1)
        tokens.insert(insert_pos, dup)

    # Occasionally prepend/append whitespace variants
    sep_variants = [" ", "  "]  # use spaces only; no tabs to remain within simple space-separated expectation
    sep = rng.choice(sep_variants)
    s = sep.join(tokens)

    if rng.random() < 0.25:
        s = (" " * rng.randint(1, 3)) + s
    if rng.random() < 0.25:
        s = s + (" " * rng.randint(1, 3))

    # Ensure non-empty and reasonable size
    s = s.strip()
    if not s:
        s = "display x11alpha bbox"

    # Truncate to max length 4000 to stay under 4096 bytes when converted to bytes
    if len(s) > 4000:
        s = s[:4000].rstrip()

    return s

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # With some probability, choose curated lists known to be valid and interesting
    curated = [
        "display x11alpha bbox",
        "pdfwrite",
        "png16m jpeg tiff24nc",
        "bbox inckov display",  # slight misspelling deliberately avoided; keep valid
        "ps2write eps2write pdfwrite",
        "tiffsep tiffsep1 tiff32nc",
        "pngalpha png16m pnggray",
    ]
    # Fix a typo in curated to ensure validity
    curated[3] = "bbox inkcov display"

    if rng.random() < 0.35:
        s = rng.choice(curated)
    else:
        s = build_device_list(rng)

    # gsapi_set_default_device_list expects bytes; use UTF-8 encoding
    data = s.encode('utf-8')
    # Guarantee non-empty
    if not data:
        data = b"display x11alpha bbox"
    # Ensure size limit
    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]
    return data

import random
import struct
import string

# Generator for Ghostscript command-line arguments suitable for gsapi_init_with_args fuzzer stub.
# We emit a single bytes buffer which the fuzz harness will split via FUZZ_PARAM_STR/FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME.
# Strategy: build a sequence of NUL-terminated strings concatenated, covering common GS options and filenames.
# Keep total size <= 4096.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

DEVICES = [
    "display", "x11", "x11alpha", "bbox", "png16m", "pnggray", "jpeg",
    "pdfwrite", "ps2write", "ppmraw", "tiff24nc", "tiffgray", "bmp16m",
]

PAPERS = [
    "a4", "letter", "legal", "a3", "tabloid", "ledger"
]

PROFILES = [
    "sRGB.icc", "SWOP.icc", "CoatedFOGRA39.icc", "JapanColor.icc"
]

FONT_PATHS = [
    "/usr/share/fonts", "/Library/Fonts", "C:/Windows/Fonts", "./fonts"
]

INPUT_FILES = [
    "test.ps", "test.eps", "test.pdf", "vector.pdf", "image.ps", "utf8.ps"
]

# Common argument templates for Ghostscript
# We will randomly pick and combine them into a small argv-like list.

def make_option_set(rng):
    opts = []

    # Randomly choose a device
    if rng.random() < 0.9:
        dev = rng.choice(DEVICES)
        opts.append(f"-sDEVICE={dev}")

    # Output file pattern
    if rng.random() < 0.9:
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            # single output
            opts.append("-sOutputFile=out.%s" % ("pdf" if rng.random() < 0.5 else "png"))
        else:
            # paged pattern
            opts.append("-sOutputFile=page-%03d.%s" % (rng.randint(1, 3), rng.choice(["png", "jpg", "tif"])) )

    # Resolution
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        dpi = rng.choice([72, 96, 150, 200, 300, 600, 1200])
        opts.append(f"-r{dpi}")

    # Paper size or width/height
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        if rng.random() < 0.6:
            opts.append(f"-sPAPERSIZE={rng.choice(PAPERS)}")
        else:
            w = rng.choice([595, 612, 842, 1191])
            h = rng.choice([842, 792, 1000, 1684])
            opts.append(f"-g{w}x{h}")

    # Color/BW flags
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        opts.append(rng.choice(["-dCOLORSCREEN", "-dNOPAUSE", "-dBATCH", "-dSAFER", "-dNOSAFER"]))

    # ICC profile or default RGB
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        opts.append(f"-sDefaultRGBProfile={rng.choice(PROFILES)}")

    # Font path
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        # build path list separator depending on platform flavor
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            sep = ";"
        else:
            sep = ":"
        parts = rng.sample(FONT_PATHS, k=rng.randint(1, min(3, len(FONT_PATHS))))
        opts.append(f"-sFONTPATH={sep.join(parts)}")

    # PDF-specific switches
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        opts.append(rng.choice([
            "-dPDFSETTINGS=/screen",
            "-dPDFSETTINGS=/ebook",
            "-dPDFSETTINGS=/printer",
            "-dDetectDuplicateImages=true",
            "-dDetectDuplicateImages=false",
            "-dDownsampleColorImages=true",
            "-dCompressFonts=true",
        ]))

    # Language selection or quiet
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        opts.append(rng.choice(["-q", "-dLANGUAGE=PostScript", "-dLANGUAGE=PDF"]))

    # Include a filename or two
    files = rng.sample(INPUT_FILES, k=rng.randint(1, min(2, len(INPUT_FILES))))
    opts.extend(files)

    # Optionally include a small inline PostScript via -c ... -f pattern
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        ps_snippets = [
            "/Times-Roman findfont 12 scalefont setfont (Hello) show showpage",
            "0 0 moveto 200 200 lineto stroke showpage",
            "100 100 translate 45 rotate (Rotated) show showpage",
        ]
        opts.append("-c")
        opts.append(rng.choice(ps_snippets))
        opts.append("-f")

    return opts


def pack_cstrings(strings):
    # Concatenate NUL-terminated strings; ensure total <= MAX_TOTAL
    out = bytearray()
    for s in strings:
        b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='strict') + b"\x00"
        if len(out) + len(b) > MAX_TOTAL:
            break
        out += b
    return bytes(out)


def random_progname(rng):
    # argv[0]
    base = rng.choice(["gs", "gswin64c", "gswin32c", "gs-fuzz"]) 
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        suffix = ''.join(rng.choices(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits, k=rng.randint(1,4)))
        base += "-" + suffix
    return base


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Build argv-like list with 1..5 extra args (fuzzer stub limits to 1..5 extra plus argv[0])
    # We will provide more than enough NUL-terminated strings; the harness will pick FUZZ_PARAM_STR
    # values from this pool.

    argv = [random_progname(rng)]

    # Create one or two groups of option sets to mix diversity
    group_count = 1 if rng.random() < 0.6 else 2
    for _ in range(group_count):
        argv.extend(make_option_set(rng))

    # Ensure inclusion of some edge-case but valid arguments
    # - empty output to stdout for some devices
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        argv.append("-sOutputFile=%stdout%")

    # -dTextAlphaBits / -dGraphicsAlphaBits
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        argv.append(f"-dTextAlphaBits={rng.choice([1,2,4])}")
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        argv.append(f"-dGraphicsAlphaBits={rng.choice([1,2,4])}")

    # Limit total number of args to something small to match stub behavior (<= 6 additional)
    # The stub itself will cap at up to 6 total including argv[0]; but it draws FUZZ_PARAM_STR
    # independently. We keep our list modest.
    if len(argv) > 12:
        argv = argv[:12]

    return pack_cstrings(argv)

# Generate valid Ghostscript-consumable buffers for string-based run APIs.
# We focus on PostScript programs (mostly ASCII), with occasional small PDFs.
# The fuzzer stubs cap string sizes to 512/1024 bytes, so we keep outputs <= 1024 bytes.

PS_PROLOGS = [
    "%!PS-Adobe-3.0\n",
    "%!PS\n",
    "%!\n",
]

PS_SNIPPETS = [
    # Simple arithmetic and stack ops
    "1 2 add =\n",
    "[1 2 3] aload pop = = =\n",
    "/x 10 def x x mul =\n",
    "(Hello, World!) print\n",
    "(unicode: \305\345) print\n",
    # Graphics setup
    "72 72 translate 144 144 scale 0 0 moveto 1 setlinewidth\n",
    "newpath 0 0 moveto 1 0 lineto 1 1 lineto 0 1 lineto closepath stroke\n",
    # Color and text
    "/Times-Roman findfont 12 scalefont setfont 0 0 moveto (GS) show\n",
    "0.2 setgray 50 50 moveto (Gray) show\n",
    # Procedures and dicts
    "/square { dup 0 rlineto dup 0 exch rlineto neg 0 rlineto closepath } def\n",
    "newpath 10 10 moveto 50 square stroke\n",
    # Conditionals and loops
    "/n 5 def 0 1 n { pop } for\n",
    # File ops with (%stdout) device
    "(%stdout) (w) file dup (Line to stdout) writestring (\n) writestring closefile\n",
    # Imaging operators setpagedevice minimal
    "<< /PageSize [300 300] >> setpagedevice\n",
    # Strings and names
    "/s (ABCDE) def s length = s 1 3 getinterval ==\n",
]

PS_TRAILERS = [
    "showpage\n",
    "flush\n",
    "\n",
]

# Minimal valid PDF generator (version 1.4) kept tiny; optionally compressed stream.
def make_minimal_pdf(rng: random.Random, target_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Build a tiny PDF with 1 page and a content stream that shows text/graphics.
    # We keep offsets correct for the objects we create. Object count small to keep size.
    # Objects: 1: Catalog, 2: Pages, 3: Page, 4: Font, 5: Contents
    content_snippets = [
        b"BT /F1 12 Tf 72 720 Td (Hello GS) Tj ET\n",
        b"0.2 g 72 700 100 20 re f\n",
        b"0 0 1 rg 72 680 100 2 re f\n",
        b"q 1 0 0 1 72 650 cm 0 0 200 100 re S Q\n",
    ]
    stream = b"".join(rng.sample(content_snippets, k=rng.randint(1, len(content_snippets))))
    use_flate = rng.random() < 0.6 and len(stream) > 0
    if use_flate:
        cdata = zlib.compress(stream)
        filter_entry = b"/Filter /FlateDecode "
        length_entry = f"/Length {len(cdata)} ".encode()
        stream_data = cdata
    else:
        filter_entry = b""
        length_entry = f"/Length {len(stream)} ".encode()
        stream_data = stream

    parts = []
    xref = []
    def add(obj: bytes) -> int:
        offset = sum(len(p) for p in parts)
        xref.append(offset)
        parts.append(obj)
        return offset

    header = b"%PDF-1.4\n%\xB5\xED\xAE\xFB\n"
    parts.append(header)

    # 1 Catalog
    add(b"1 0 obj\n<< /Type /Catalog /Pages 2 0 R >>\nendobj\n")
    # 2 Pages
    add(b"2 0 obj\n<< /Type /Pages /Kids [3 0 R] /Count 1 >>\nendobj\n")
    # 3 Page
    add(b"3 0 obj\n<< /Type /Page /Parent 2 0 R /MediaBox [0 0 612 792] /Contents 5 0 R /Resources << /Font << /F1 4 0 R >> >> >>\nendobj\n")
    # 4 Font
    add(b"4 0 obj\n<< /Type /Font /Subtype /Type1 /BaseFont /Helvetica >>\nendobj\n")
    # 5 Contents
    stream_obj = b"5 0 obj\n<< " + length_entry + filter_entry + b" >>\nstream\n" + stream_data + b"\nendstream\nendobj\n"
    add(stream_obj)

    xref_start = sum(len(p) for p in parts)
    # xref table
    count = 6  # including object 0
    xref_entries = [b"0000000000 65535 f \n"]
    # We need offsets for objects 1..5; we recorded offsets after header. Compute true offsets: header at 0.
    # xref list order: 1..5
    # We recompute by scanning parts concatenation to find "1 0 obj" etc. Simpler: track via xref recorded offsets after header.
    # We recorded offsets as absolute in parts, so adjust? The first add offset was len(header) at that time. That's correct absolute.
    for off in xref:
        xref_entries.append(f"{off:010d} 00000 n \n".encode())
    xref_section = b"xref\n0 %d\n" % count + b"".join(xref_entries)

    trailer = (
        b"trailer\n<< /Size %d /Root 1 0 R >>\nstartxref\n%d\n%%%%EOF\n" % (count, xref_start)
    )

    pdf = b"".join(parts) + xref_section + trailer

    # Trim or pad (rarely) to target_len boundary if requested
    if target_len and len(pdf) > target_len:
        return pdf[:target_len]
    return pdf


def make_postscript(rng: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    prolog = rng.choice(PS_PROLOGS)
    body = []

    # Occasionally build a chunked program suitable for run_string_continue
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        # Create balanced fragments ending with tokens that encourage NeedInput when chunked
        fragments = [
            "{ ",
            "100 1 5 { pop } for ",
            "(Chunk) print ",
            "dup 2 mul ",
            "} if\n",
        ]
        rng.shuffle(fragments)
        body.append("".join(fragments))

    # Insert a random selection of snippets
    k = rng.randint(2, 6)
    snippets = rng.sample(PS_SNIPPETS, k=min(k, len(PS_SNIPPETS)))
    body.extend(snippets)

    # Optionally define and use a parsed parameter-like dictionary to trigger setpagedevice behaviors
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        pages = rng.choice([[612, 792], [595, 842], [300, 300], [242, 242]])
        body.append(f"<< /PageSize [{pages[0]} {pages[1]}] /Orientation 0 >> setpagedevice\n")

    trailer = rng.choice(PS_TRAILERS)
    program = prolog + "".join(body) + trailer

    # Ensure size constraints
    b = program.encode('latin1', errors='replace')
    if len(b) > max_len:
        b = b[:max_len]
    return b


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Decide format: PostScript (70%) or minimal PDF (30%)
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        max_len = rng.choice([256, 384, 512, 768, 1024])
        return make_postscript(rng, max_len)
    else:
        target_len = rng.choice([0, 512, 768, 1024])
        return make_minimal_pdf(rng, target_len)

import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List, Tuple

# This generator creates a realistic Ghostscript input document as bytes.
# The target fuzzer stub uses FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME, so the bytes produced here
# will be written by the harness into a file and the filename passed to gsapi_run_file.
# We aim to produce valid documents across several formats Ghostscript supports:
# - PostScript (PS)
# - Encapsulated PostScript (EPS)
# - PDF (minimal but valid, with cross-reference and trailer)
# - Plain text PostScript program snippets exercising operators
# - Simple DSC-compliant multi-page PS
# The selection is randomized but seeded. Sizes remain <= 4096 bytes.

MAX_SIZE = 4096


def _rand(r: random.Random, a: int, b: int) -> int:
    return r.randint(a, b)


def _choose(r: random.Random, seq):
    return seq[_rand(r, 0, len(seq) - 1)]


def _ps_header(r: random.Random) -> str:
    dsc = [
        "%!PS-Adobe-3.0\n",
        "%!PS-Adobe-2.0\n",
        "%!\n",
    ]
    return _choose(r, dsc)


def _ps_prolog_common() -> str:
    return (
        "%%Creator: fuzzgen\n"
        "%%LanguageLevel: 3\n"
        "%%Pages: (atend)\n"
        "%%BoundingBox: 0 0 595 842\n"
        "%%EndComments\n"
    )


def _ps_page(page_num: int, content: str) -> str:
    return (
        f"%%Page: {page_num} {page_num}\n"
        "gsave\n"
        + content +
        "grestore\nshowpage\n"
    )


def _ps_footer(pages: int) -> str:
    return f"%%Trailer\n%%Pages: {pages}\n%%EOF\n"


def _ps_content_variant(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Produce varied but valid PS content that exercises common operators
    snippets: List[str] = []

    # Set up fonts and draw text
    text = [
        "/Helvetica findfont 20 scalefont setfont 72 720 moveto (Hello, Ghostscript!) show\n",
        "/Courier findfont 12 scalefont setfont 72 700 moveto (Fuzzing valid PS) show\n",
    ]

    # Vector graphics
    graphics = [
        "newpath 100 600 moveto 200 600 lineto 200 700 lineto closepath 0.9 setgray fill\n",
        "0 setgray 2 setlinewidth newpath 100 580 moveto 300 580 lineto stroke\n",
        "0.1 0.5 0.8 setrgbcolor newpath 150 500 40 0 360 arc fill 0 setgray\n",
        "newpath 72 500 moveto 144 540 lineto 72 580 lineto closepath 0.2 setgray fill 0 setgray\n",
    ]

    # Images (simple 1x1 or small image to stay valid and small)
    image_snip = [
        "% image 2x2\n"
        "gsave 300 700 translate 2 2 scale\n"
        "2 2 8 [2 0 0 -2 0 2] {<FF0000FF>} image grestore\n",
    ]

    # Procedures and stack operations
    procs = [
        "/square { dup mul } bind def 4 square pop\n",
        "/joinstr { exch =only ( ) print = } def (A) (B) joinstr\n",
    ]

    snippets.extend(text)
    snippets.extend(r.sample(graphics, k=_rand(r, 1, len(graphics))))
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        snippets.append(_choose(r, image_snip))
    if r.random() < 0.6:
        snippets.append(_choose(r, procs))

    # Color spaces and gsave/grestore nesting
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        snippets.append("gsave 0.3 setgray 72 640 moveto (Gray text) show grestore\n")
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        snippets.append("/DeviceRGB setcolorspace 0 1 0 setcolor 72 620 moveto (Green) show\n")

    return "".join(snippets)


def _generate_ps(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    pages = _rand(r, 1, 3)
    doc = [_ps_header(r), _ps_prolog_common()]
    for p in range(1, pages + 1):
        content = _ps_content_variant(r)
        doc.append(_ps_page(p, content))
    doc.append(_ps_footer(pages))
    data = "".join(doc).encode("latin-1")
    return data[:MAX_SIZE]


def _generate_eps(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    header = "%!PS-Adobe-3.0 EPSF-3.0\n"
    bbox = "%%BoundingBox: 0 0 300 300\n"
    body = (
        "%%Creator: fuzzgen\n%%EndComments\n"
        "gsave\n72 72 translate\n0.2 0.6 0.9 setrgbcolor\nnewpath 0 0 moveto 200 0 lineto 200 200 lineto closepath fill\n0 setgray 10 setlinewidth newpath 0 0 moveto 200 200 lineto stroke\n/Helvetica findfont 18 scalefont setfont 10 220 moveto (EPS) show\n" 
        "grestore\n%%EOF\n"
    )
    data = (header + bbox + body).encode("latin-1")
    return data[:MAX_SIZE]


def _pdf_escape(s: str) -> str:
    return s.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace("(", "\\(").replace(")", "\\)")


def _generate_pdf(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Minimal but valid PDF 1.4 with 1-2 pages, a Catalog, Pages, Page, Contents stream
    # Build objects dynamically and construct xref
    title = _pdf_escape(_choose(r, ["Fuzz PDF", "Ghostscript Test", "Valid PDF Sample"]))

    objects: List[Tuple[int, bytes]] = []
    obj_id = 1

    def add_object(content: bytes) -> int:
        nonlocal obj_id
        objects.append((obj_id, content))
        obj_id += 1
        return obj_id - 1

    # 1: Catalog
    # 2: Pages
    # 3..: Page(s)
    # N: Font
    # M: Content stream
    font_obj = add_object(b"<< /Type /Font /Subtype /Type1 /Name /F1 /BaseFont /Helvetica >>\n")

    contents_texts = []
    for i in range(_rand(r, 1, 2)):
        txt = _choose(r, [
            "BT /F1 24 Tf 72 720 Td (Hello Ghostscript) Tj ET\n",
            "BT /F1 12 Tf 72 700 Td (PDF valid content) Tj ET\n",
            "BT /F1 18 Tf 100 600 Td (Fuzzing) Tj ET\n",
        ])
        contents_texts.append(txt)

    streams = []
    stream_objs = []
    for txt in contents_texts:
        stream_data = txt.encode("latin-1")
        stream = b"<< /Length " + str(len(stream_data)).encode() + b" >>\nstream\n" + stream_data + b"endstream\n"
        sid = add_object(stream)
        stream_objs.append(sid)
        streams.append(stream)

    pages_kids = []
    page_objs = []
    pages_obj_placeholder = 0  # will be replaced

    for sid in stream_objs:
        page = (
            b"<< /Type /Page /Parent 2 0 R /MediaBox [0 0 595 842]"
            b" /Resources << /Font << /F1 " + str(font_obj).encode() + b" 0 R >> >>"
            b" /Contents " + str(sid).encode() + b" 0 R >>\n"
        )
        pid = add_object(page)
        page_objs.append(pid)
        pages_kids.append(f"{pid} 0 R")

    pages = ("<< /Type /Pages /Kids [" + " ".join(pages_kids) + "] /Count " + str(len(page_objs)) + " >>\n").encode("latin-1")
    # Insert Pages at obj 2
    objects.insert(1, (2, pages))

    catalog = b"<< /Type /Catalog /Pages 2 0 R >>\n"
    objects.insert(0, (1, catalog))

    # Re-number is consistent (we inserted fixed IDs), build file
    header = b"%PDF-1.4\n%\xE2\xE3\xCF\xD3\n"
    body = bytearray()
    xref_positions = {}

    def write_obj(obj_num: int, content: bytes):
        xref_positions[obj_num] = len(header) + len(body)
        body.extend(f"{obj_num} 0 obj\n".encode("ascii"))
        body.extend(content)
        body.extend(b"endobj\n")

    for obj_num, content in objects:
        write_obj(obj_num, content)

    xref_start = len(header) + len(body)
    highest_obj = max(num for num, _ in objects)
    xref = bytearray()
    xref.extend(b"xref\n")
    xref.extend(f"0 {highest_obj+1}\n".encode("ascii"))
    # entry 0 (free)
    xref.extend(b"0000000000 65535 f \n")
    for i in range(1, highest_obj + 1):
        pos = xref_positions.get(i, 0)
        xref.extend(f"{pos:010d} 00000 n \n".encode("ascii"))

    trailer = (
        b"trailer\n" +
        (b"<< /Size " + str(highest_obj + 1).encode() + b" /Root 1 0 R >>\n") +
        b"startxref\n" + str(xref_start).encode() + b"\n%%EOF\n"
    )

    pdf = header + body + xref + trailer
    return pdf[:MAX_SIZE]


def _generate_dsc_multipage_ps(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    header = "%!PS-Adobe-3.0\n" + _ps_prolog_common()
    pages = _rand(r, 2, 4)
    body = []
    for p in range(1, pages + 1):
        content = (
            f"%%Page: {p} {p}\n"
            "/Times-Roman findfont 14 scalefont setfont\n"
            f"72 700 moveto (Page {p}) show\n"
            "newpath 72 680 200 40 0 360 arc stroke\n"
            "showpage\n"
        )
        body.append(content)
    trailer = _ps_footer(pages)
    data = (header + "".join(body) + trailer).encode("latin-1")
    return data[:MAX_SIZE]


def _generate_text_ps_program(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # A compact PS program that performs arithmetic and stack ops
    prog = (
        "%!\n"
        "/F {/Helvetica findfont exch scalefont setfont} def\n"
        "24 F 72 760 moveto (Computation) show\n"
        "10 20 add 2 div dup\n"
        " /Times-Roman findfont 12 scalefont setfont 72 740 moveto\n"
        " (Result: ) show dup 20 string cvs show\n"
        "0 0 1 setrgbcolor 100 700 moveto (Blue) show 0 setgray\n"
        "newpath 200 680 30 0 360 arc fill\nshowpage\n"
    )
    return prog.encode("latin-1")[:MAX_SIZE]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    # Prefer PDFs and PS to exercise different parsers; weighted choice
    producers = [
        (_generate_pdf, 3),
        (_generate_ps, 3),
        (_generate_eps, 1),
        (_generate_dsc_multipage_ps, 2),
        (_generate_text_ps_program, 2),
    ]
    weighted: List = []
    for fn, w in producers:
        weighted.extend([fn] * w)
    fn = _choose(r, weighted)
    data = fn(r)
    # Ensure non-empty and within size
    if not data:
        data = b"%! Empty but valid PS\nshowpage\n"
    return data[:MAX_SIZE]

import random
import string

# Generator for Ghostscript parameter strings used by gsapi_set_param fuzzer.
# We focus on producing valid and interesting NUL-terminated strings that act as
# parameter values for gs_spt_name/string/parsed. The harness caps strings to 256 bytes.
# We therefore build diverse yet valid strings <= 256 chars.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096
MAX_STR = 256

# A collection of interesting Ghostscript parameter payloads. These are values, not keys.
INTERESTING_VALUES = [
    # Device names
    "display", "x11", "x11alpha", "bbox", "ppmraw", "png16m", "jpeg", "pdfwrite",
    # Page sizes and media names
    "A4", "A3", "Letter", "Legal", "Tabloid", "11x17", "A5", "A6",
    # PageSize as parsed array string (for gs_spt_parsed)
    "[595 842]",  # A4 in points
    "[612 792]",  # Letter
    "[841.89 1190.55]",
    # Resolution
    "72", "96", "150", "300", "600", "1200",
    # Boolean-like strings
    "true", "false", "True", "False", "YES", "NO",
    # Color models / separations
    "DeviceRGB", "DeviceCMYK", "Gray", "DeviceGray", "sRGB",
    # PDF settings
    "/screen", "/ebook", "/printer", "/prepress", "/default",
    # Fonts and related
    "Courier", "Helvetica", "Times-Roman", "Symbol",
    # Paper trays / media sources
    "Upper", "Lower", "Middle", "Manual",
    # File paths and patterns
    "%stdout", "%stderr", "%pipe%cat", "/tmp/out.png", "C:/temp/out.pdf", "-",
    # ICC profiles / color intents
    "RelativeColorimetric", "Perceptual", "AbsoluteColorimetric", "Saturation",
    # Password-like
    "ownerpass", "userpass",
    # Language switches
    "PS", "PDF", "EPS",
    # Datetime-like
    "20240101", "19991231",
    # Locale/encoding indicators
    "UTF-8", "UTF16-LE",
]

# Some parameter keys accept name values that start with '/' (PostScript name syntax).
SLASHABLE = [
    "DeviceRGB", "DeviceCMYK", "Gray", "DeviceGray", "sRGB",
    "screen", "ebook", "printer", "prepress", "default",
    "Courier", "Helvetica", "Times-Roman", "Symbol",
]

# Generate numeric sequences as strings (useful for parameters expecting numeric-in-string)
def gen_numeric_str(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        return str(rng.randint(-100000, 100000))
    else:
        val = rng.uniform(-1e6, 1e6)
        return ("%.4f" % val).rstrip("0").rstrip(".")

# Generate bracketed arrays suitable for gs_spt_parsed strings (e.g., for PageSize)
def gen_parsed_array(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(2, 6)
    parts = []
    for _ in range(n):
        if rng.random() < 0.7:
            parts.append(gen_numeric_str(rng))
        else:
            name = rng.choice(["/DeviceRGB", "/DeviceCMYK", "/Gray", "/Image", "/Text"]) \
                   if rng.random() < 0.4 else gen_numeric_str(rng)
            parts.append(name)
    s = "[" + " ".join(parts) + "]"
    return s[:MAX_STR]

# Generate a path-like string
def gen_path(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        parts = ["/", "tmp", rng.choice(["out", "in", "test", "gs"]) + str(rng.randint(0, 999))]
        base = "/".join([p.strip("/") for p in parts])
        ext = rng.choice([".ps", ".pdf", ".png", ".jpg", ".tif"]) if rng.random() < 0.7 else ""
        return base + ext
    else:
        drive = rng.choice(list("CDE"))
        folders = ["temp", "gs", "work", "docs"]
        base = f"{drive}:/" + "/".join([rng.choice(folders), rng.choice(folders)])
        name = rng.choice(["file", "out", "input"]) + str(rng.randint(0, 999))
        ext = rng.choice([".ps", ".pdf", ".png", ".jpg", ".tif"]) if rng.random() < 0.7 else ""
        return base + "/" + name + ext

# Generate a general "word" token
def gen_word(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    alph = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_"
    n = rng.randint(1, 20)
    return "".join(rng.choice(alph) for _ in range(n))

# Generate a composite PostScript-like dictionary or sequence for gs_spt_parsed
def gen_parsed_snippet(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    t = rng.random()
    if t < 0.4:
        return gen_parsed_array(rng)
    elif t < 0.7:
        entries = []
        m = rng.randint(1, 4)
        for _ in range(m):
            key = "/" + gen_word(rng)
            if rng.random() < 0.5:
                val = gen_numeric_str(rng)
            else:
                val = "/" + gen_word(rng)
            entries.append(f"{key} {val}")
        s = "<< " + " ".join(entries) + " >>"
        return s[:MAX_STR]
    else:
        parts = []
        k = rng.randint(2, 8)
        for _ in range(k):
            choice = rng.random()
            if choice < 0.4:
                parts.append(gen_numeric_str(rng))
            elif choice < 0.7:
                parts.append("/" + gen_word(rng))
            else:
                parts.append(gen_word(rng))
        s = " ".join(parts)
        return s[:MAX_STR]

# Build a value string aiming to cover string/name/parsed usages.
def build_value(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    mode = rng.randint(0, 6)
    if mode == 0:
        v = rng.choice(INTERESTING_VALUES)
        if v in SLASHABLE and rng.random() < 0.7 and not v.startswith("/"):
            v = "/" + v
        return v[:MAX_STR]
    elif mode == 1:
        return gen_numeric_str(rng)[:MAX_STR]
    elif mode == 2:
        return gen_parsed_array(rng)
    elif mode == 3:
        return gen_path(rng)[:MAX_STR]
    elif mode == 4:
        words = [gen_word(rng) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 5))]
        return " ".join(words)[:MAX_STR]
    elif mode == 5:
        return gen_parsed_snippet(rng)
    else:
        devs = [rng.choice(["display", "x11", "x11alpha", "bbox", "ppmraw", "png16m"]) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 4))]
        return " ".join(devs)[:MAX_STR]

# Construct the final byte buffer with multiple NUL-terminated strings.

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    count = rng.randint(2, 6)

    strings = []
    total_size = 1  # for count byte

    for _ in range(count):
        s = build_value(rng)
        s = s.replace("\x00", "")
        if not s:
            s = "A4"
        b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
        if len(b) > MAX_STR:
            b = b[:MAX_STR]
        if total_size + len(b) + 1 > MAX_TOTAL:
            avail = MAX_TOTAL - total_size - 1
            b = b[:max(0, avail)]
        strings.append(b)
        total_size += len(b) + 1
        if total_size >= MAX_TOTAL:
            break

    out = bytearray()
    out.append(len(strings) & 0xFF)
    for b in strings:
        out.extend(b)
        out.append(0)

    if not out:
        out = bytearray(b"\x01A4\x00")

    return bytes(out)
